item.title: US woman says co-op staff took her pets, hid dog's whereabouts; court allows lawsuit
item.description: A New York woman who accused co-op employees of entering her apartment without permission, removing her dog and cat, and concealing her dog's whereabouts can continue pursuing two legal claims. Nearly three years after the incident, an appeals court allowed her trespass and emotional distress claims to proceed. Court records indicated that her dog was euthanised after spending nearly two months at a shelter.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Titanic's owners received $5 million within 30 days of the sinking; 114 years later, original insurance certificate resurfaces and could sell for $67,000
item.description: An authentic insurance document related to the Titanic's last journey is slated for auction in Britain. This significant paperwork details the insurance sought mere weeks before the 1912 sinking. The owners received their payout shortly after the tragedy, contrasting sharply with the delays faced by bereaved families. The piece also underscores the important insurance arrangements for the Titanic, along with a selection of other artifacts that commemorate its storied past.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Small Listing Spurs Protection: Indiana saves 3,950 acres; new wildlife area opens
item.description: An effort to save a 191-acre parcel in Indiana led to the protection of nearly 4,000 acres. The land was acquired to prevent fragmentation and protect wildlife habitats in the area. Various organizations and public agencies collaborated to complete the acquisition. The Busseron Creek Fish and Wildlife Area opened to the public in April 2025 for outdoor recreation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Russell Brand Trial: Jury weighs seven sexual offence charges; deliberations to resume Wednesday
item.description: Jury discussions are now underway regarding comedian Russell Brand's sexual offences trial at Southwark Crown Court. Faced with multiple charges from six women about occurrences between 1999 and 2009, the prosecution argues that Brand leveraged his celebrity status for sexual manipulation. In his defense, Brand asserts that all encounters were consensual and refutes the allegations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: David Bowie performed here, Carlos Sainz raced go-karts: Madrid's iconic La Ermita mall demolished for 529 homes in €77 million makeover
item.description: The once-thriving La Ermita shopping centre in Madrid has met its end as plans to demolish it progress. In its place, a new development will rise, offering 529 homes, a blend of accessible and protected housing. This initiative aims to enhance local infrastructure, incorporating public spaces and green zones for the community.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Australia launches A$28 million project to stop invasive cane toads from reaching Pilbara after 1935 introduction
item.description: A new project involving Curtin University and Rio Tinto seeks to establish a waterless barrier for cane toads. The initiative intends to protect Western Australia's Pilbara area from the ecologically damaging species. Researchers plan to modify water sources over a significant area to prevent the toads' survival. Traditional Owners have been engaged throughout the project to ensure cultural significance is respected.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Did Russia rehearse satellite attack? Expert on close encounter with western spacecraft
item.description: A Russian military satellite's recent close encounter with a commercial satellite has sparked serious concerns about security in space. Experts are alarmed, suggesting this action may signal an escalation towards targeting satellites linked to military operations. US officials have warned that these provocative moves could jeopardize commercial satellite networks, further fueling the existing geopolitical tensions and prompting analysts to rigorously track Russian movements in the sky.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Kanye West's 6,713-acre Wyoming ranch returns to family that owned it for generations
item.description: In 2019, Kanye West acquired the Bighorn Mountain Ranch, visualizing it as an exclusive retreat. However, with shifting priorities, the Flitner family reacquired the property in 2025. Concerns over potential subdivision led them to prioritize agricultural preservation and landscape protection, ensuring that historic structures could be restored and serve as a lasting connection to the land for future generations.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Woman's wedding falls apart, 11 strangers join her for a 'non-wedding' in Northern Ireland
item.description: After her fiance suffered a medical emergency and their wedding plans fell apart, Bridget Devaney invited 11 women she had never met to join her on a trip to Northern Ireland. The women, from the US, Canada and Wales, spent a week exploring popular attractions and celebrating her 'non-wedding'. What began as an online invitation turned into unexpected friendships and plans for future trips.

item.title: NASA’s 3,200-pound Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth over Indonesia after failed $30 million rescue mission
item.description: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered Earth's atmosphere after 22 years in orbit, ending its mission. Swift was crucial for understanding gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic events, detecting over 2,000 bursts. The spacecraft's orbit deteriorated due to increased solar activity, leading to its uncontrolled descent. NASA attempted a rescue operation, but it ultimately failed, resulting in its re-entry on November 4, 2026.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Detroit man turns two rubber bands into 11,578-pound ball, breaking Guinness World Record after 11 years
item.description: Claude P. Moore began his rubber band ball project in 2015, starting with two rubber bands. Over eleven years, he built the ball to an impressive 11,578 pounds, surpassing the previous record. Friends and family supported him throughout this extensive journey, helping transport the enormous ball for its official measurement. The record was confirmed in August 2026 by Guinness World Records during a public ceremony.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Filipino engineer wins £30,000 award for sensor that detects hidden earthquake damage in buildings
item.description: A Filipino structural engineer has won the 2026 James Dyson Global Sustainability Award and £30,000 for developing Sentinel, a sensor that detects hidden damage in buildings after earthquakes. Developed by Aldrei Ong, the technology uses self-sensing concrete to identify cracks and monitor structural changes. The invention could help engineers assess potentially unsafe buildings more quickly and reduce the risk of collapse.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nine people set out for a one-hour boat trip in Micronesia; three months and 5,400 km later, villagers in Kiribati rescued five survivors
item.description: In July, a boat with nine individuals vanished during its voyage between islands in Micronesia. The US Coast Guard launched a ten-day search, but no clues were found. Miraculously, nearly three months later, five survivors emerged on a Kiribati island, a staggering 5,400 kilometers from where they set sail. After enduring severe dehydration and malnutrition, they received medical attention.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Joshua Wong Sentencing: activist gets fresh 10-year NSL term; warns against dissent
item.description: Joshua Wong has been sentenced to 10 years in prison under Hong Kong's national security laws, adding to his existing sentence from another political case. His imprisonment highlights the government's determination to suppress dissent, particularly targeting his international campaigns for democracy. Yet, despite being behind bars, Wong continues to inspire a new generation of pro-democracy advocates in Hong Kong.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma
